column2: “工具能把活干好就行，不必执着于细枝末节。”

column1: A skilled warrior is a beautiful sight to behold.
column2: “武艺高强的战士，令人赏心悦目。”

column1: Why this obsession with weapons and battle?  I don't understand some people.
column2: “为什么如此痴迷武器与战斗？有些人真让我不理解。”

column1: The world isn't always safe.  I can see the value in martial training, the beauty even, but it shouldn't be exalted.
column2: “这世界并不总是安全的。我明白习武的价值，甚至它的美，但不该将它奉为至高。”

column1: We should all be so lucky as to truly master a skill.
column2: “但愿我们都能有幸真正精通一门技艺。”

column1: The amount of practice that goes into mastering a skill is so impressive.
column2: “精通一门技艺所付出的磨炼，实在令人敬佩。”

column1: Everyone should broaden their horizons.  Any work beyond learning the basics is just a waste.
column2: “人人都应拓宽眼界。掌握基础之后再花功夫，只是浪费。”

column1: All of that practice is misspent effort.
I think people should hone their skills, but it's possible to take it too far and lose sight of the breadth of life.
column2: “人应当磨炼技艺，但太过投入，也会忽略生活的广阔。”

column1: There's more to life than becoming great at just one thing, but being good at several isn't bad!
column2: “人生不只有精通一件事，多擅长几样也不错！”

column1: In life, you should work hard.  Then work harder.
column2: “人生在世，应当努力，再更加努力。”

column1: Hard work is the true sign of character.
The best way to get what you want out of life is to work for it.
column2: “想过上自己要的生活，最好的办法就是为之努力。”

column1: It's foolish to work hard for anything.
column2: “为任何事辛苦劳作，都是愚蠢的。”

column1: You shouldn't whittle your life away on working.
column2: “不该把一生都消磨在劳作上。”

column1: Hard work is bested by luck, connections and wealth every time.
column2: “苦干从来比不上运气、人脉与财富。”

column1: An earnest effort at any required tasks.  That's all that's needed.
column2: “把该做的事认真做完，就够了。”

column1: I only work so hard, but sometimes you have to do what you have to do.
column2: “我干活只肯出这么多力，但有些事该做还是得做。”

column1: Hard work is great.  Finding a way to work half as hard is even better.
column2: “勤劳固然好，找到省一半力气的办法更好。”

column1: We must be ready to sacrifice when the time comes.
column2: “到了需要的时候，我们必须甘愿牺牲。”

column1: Why harm yourself for anybody else's benefit?
column2: “何必为了别人的好处损害自己？”

column1: Some self-sacrifice is worthy, but do not forget yourself in devotion to the well-being of others.
column2: “适当牺牲自己值得敬重，但为他人谋福祉，也别忘了自己。”

column1: It's a competitive world, and you'd be a fool to think otherwise.
column2: “这世界处处都是竞争，不承认这一点才是愚蠢。”

column1: All of this striving against one another is so foolish.
column2: “这些相互争胜的举动，实在愚蠢。”

column1: There is value in a good rivalry, but such danger as well.
column2: “有个好对手固然可贵，但竞争也暗藏危险。”

column1: Anybody that sticks to something a moment longer than they have to is an idiot.
column2: “没必要再坚持，却还多耗一刻的人，都是傻子。”

column1: It's good to keep pushing forward, but sometimes you just have to know when it's time to stop.
column2: “不断向前固然好，但有时也要懂得适可而止。”

column1: Wouldn't it be grand to just take my life off and do nothing for the rest of my days?
column2: “若能从此歇下，余生什么也不做，岂不美好？”

column1: It's best to slow down and just relax.
Time spent in leisure is such a waste.
There's some value in leisure, but one also has to engage with other aspects of life.
column2: “闲暇有其益处，但生活的其他方面也不能荒废。”

column1: Trade is the life-blood of a thriving society.
All of this buying and selling isn't honest work.
column2: “这些买进卖出的营生，算不上踏实劳动。”

column1: There's something to be said for trade as a necessity, but there are better things in life to do with one's time.
column2: “贸易确有必要，但人生还有更值得花时间的事。”

column1: There's nothing like a great romance!
column2: “没有什么比得上一场美好的爱情！”

column1: These people carrying on about romance should be more practical.
column2: “这些满口爱情的人，该实际一点。”

column1: You shouldn't get too carried away with romance, but it's fine in moderation.
column2: “别为爱情过于忘形，适度就好。”

column1: It's wonderful to be out exploring the wilds!
I could do without all of those creatures and that tangled greenery.
column2: “那些生物和纠缠的草木，我宁可都不要。”

column1: Nature can be enjoyed and used for myriad purposes, but there must always be respect and even fear of its power.
column2: “自然可供欣赏，也有无数用途，但对它的力量，始终要怀有尊重，乃至畏惧。”

column1: Let there be peace throughout the world.
How I long for the beautiful spectacle of war!
column2: “我多么向往战争那壮美的景象！”

column1: War is sometimes necessary, but peace must be valued as well, when we can have it.
column2: “战争有时不可避免，但能享有和平时，也应当珍惜。”

column1: It's a great day to fall in love all over again.
column2: “今天真是重新坠入爱河的好日子。”

column1: People do get so carried away sometimes, but not I.
column2: “人有时会忘乎所以，但我不会。”

column1: Sometimes I just don't like somebody.
How can someone be so consumed by hate?
column2: “一个人怎么会被仇恨吞噬到这种地步？”

column1: I don't understand how somebody can become so obsessed by what somebody else has.
column2: “我不明白，一个人怎么会如此执着于别人拥有的东西。”

column1: Is there something to be happy about?
It really gets me down sometimes.
I have trouble controlling my temper.
People can be so angry, and I just don't understand it.
column2: “人怎么会有那么大的怒气，我实在不理解。”

column1: W... worried?  Do I look worried?
There's nothing to be upset about.
I just don't understand these flames of passion people go on about.
column2: “人们总说欲火难耐，我实在无法理解。”

column1: I'm at my best under pressure.
column2: “有压力时，我反而发挥得最好。”

column1: Yes, I want more.  Is that so bad?
column2: “是，我想要更多。这有那么糟吗？”

column1: Why are they so fixated on these baubles?
column2: “他们为什么如此痴迷这些小玩意？”

column1: Sometimes I think I need a drink, but I can control myself.
column2: “有时我觉得该喝一杯，但我能克制自己。”

column1: There's nothing like a good brawl.
column2: “没有什么比得上痛快打上一架。”

column1: Get me going and I won't stop for anything.
column2: “只要我行动起来，就没有什么能让我停下。”

column1: Maybe I give up too early sometimes.
I don't always do things in the most efficient way.
column2: “我做事并不总是那么有效率。”

column1: We must be careful not to waste.
I don't mind stirring things up.
It's so great when everybody just gets along.
I try to live and behave properly.
column2: “我尽量让生活和言行合乎规矩。”
“所谓合乎规矩的生活，究竟是什么？”

column1: I was never one to follow advice.
I'm not much of a decision maker.
Bravery is not a strength of mine.
I don't think I'm cut out for this.
column2: “我觉得自己不适合做这件事。”

column1: Some people are so wrapped up in themselves.
I don't feel like I need to chase anything.
column2: “我觉得自己没有什么非追求不可的东西。”

column1: One should always return a favor.
It's not a gift if you expect something in return.
column2: “若是指望回报，那就不算馈赠。”

column1: I wouldn't feel comfortable getting all dressed up.
column2: “打扮得太讲究，会让我不自在。”

column1: You shouldn't waste your life on revenge.
I am a very, very important person.
column2: “我是个非常、非常重要的人物。”

column1: There's no room for mercy in this world.
Show some mercy now and again.
I'm feeling optimistic about the future.
I don't feel like telling you about it.
I could tell you all about it!
column2: “我可以把来龙去脉都告诉你！”

column1: If you have a task, do it properly.
It's not perfect, but it's good enough.  Why fret about it?
column2: “虽然不完美，但已经够好了，何必为此烦恼？”

column1: I'm not going to change my mind.
Everybody has their own way of life.
I don't understand why they have to be that way.
column2: “我不理解，他们为什么非要那样。”

column1: I don't really get attached to people.
Don't bother trying to play on my emotions.
I don't like being obligated to anybody.
Oh, I don't usually think much.
One must always carefully consider the correct course of action.
column2: “做事之前，总应慎重考虑怎样才妥当。”

column1: Everything just so in its proper place!
My trust is earned, and not by many.
column2: “想得到我的信任，得有真凭实据，而做到的人不多。”

column1: It's such a joy to be with people.
People should listen to what I have to say.
I need some more excitement in my life.
I'd just as soon not have anything too exciting happen today.
column2: “我倒希望今天别发生什么太刺激的事。”

column1: Do you have dreams?  Tell me a story!
Try to focus on the practical side of the matter.
column2: “尽量多考虑事情实际的一面。”

column1: I encountered a fascinating conundrum recently.
column2: “我最近遇到了一个引人入胜的难题。”

column1: A great piece of art is one that moves me.

I cannot stand the world any longer...

column2: “所有事情一下子全压过来了！”

column1: I'm feel like I'm about to snap.

I can't take much more of this!
